name: Chris Van Hollen

issue_poll.name: Goucher College Poll, Sept 8–12, 2022; Washington Post–UMD Poll, Sept 22–27, 2022; Baltimore Sun/University of Baltimore (OpinionWorks), Oct 20–23, 2022
issue_poll.note: Combined: Goucher top-three issue shares (economy/taxes 64, crime 62, schools 60, infrastructure 35, environment 28, housing 26); Post-UMD most important issue (economy 24, democracy 20, crime 14, education 14, abortion 11, taxes 8; https://bsos.umd.edu/featured-content/umd-post-poll-wes-moore-voters-preferred-pick-maryland-governor); Sun/UB motivating issue (inflation 11, Roe 11, crime 6, health care 3; https://www.governing.com/now/hot-button-issues-drive-maryland-voters-to-the-polls). Goucher and Post-UMD questions were asked about the governor's race.

issues.position: Raise wages and benefits; lower drug and child care costs
issues.note: Direction only; no specific economic measure named.

issues.position: Fund mental health responders for some 911 calls
issues.note: Community-Based Response Act never reached a Senate floor vote this term.
No Senate floor vote on universal pre-K this term.

issues.position: Codify Roe v. Wade in federal law

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

votes.bill_title: Disapproval of VA reproductive health services rule
votes.question: Motion to proceed

issues.position: Pass the DISCLOSE Act; end the filibuster
issues.note: No floor vote found on the DISCLOSE Act or a filibuster rules change this term.

issues.position: Close tax breaks for the wealthy and offshore profits
issues.note: H.R.1 extended 2017 tax cuts, including for high earners and corporations.

issues.position: Expand clean energy; make polluters pay cleanup costs
Let Medicare negotiate prescription drug prices
issues.note: H.R.1 widened the orphan-drug exemption from Medicare negotiation (https://www.biospace.com/policy/trumps-tax-law-restores-orphan-drug-exemptions-cuts-medicaid-threatens-340b-program-and-gives-pbms-a-pass).

caveats: No single Maryland poll ranked issues for the Senate race; ranking combines three 2022 state polls, two asked about the governor's race.
Low-profile race with no debates found; several positions come from his Feb 2022 filing release rather than fall campaign coverage.
Taxes, climate and health care are all rated on the single H.R.1 passage vote.
Absence of a floor vote on the DISCLOSE Act or filibuster change was not confirmed against senate.gov (blocked).
